scheme_name: Sarna /Jahersthan/Hadgadi & Masna Protection and Development Scheme
description:
The Sarna / Jahersthan / Hadgadi & Masna Protection and Development Scheme is a significant initiative launched by the Government of India aimed at the socio-economic upliftment of specific tribal communities in the country.

This scheme was officially launched on January 1, 2021.

It primarily focuses on the protection and development of the Sarna, Jahersthan, Hadgadi, and Masna communities.

These communities are recognized as Scheduled Tribes under the Constitution of India.

The primary objective of this scheme is to enhance the living standards of these tribal populations.

The scheme aims to provide financial assistance for various developmental activities.

It also seeks to promote education, health, and livelihood opportunities among these communities.

The measurable targets include increasing the literacy rate among these communities by at least 20% over five years.

Additionally, the scheme aims to reduce poverty levels in these communities by 30% within the same timeframe.

The benefits under this scheme include direct financial assistance of up to INR 50,000 for each eligible family.

This financial assistance can be utilized for setting up small businesses or for educational purposes.

The scheme also provides for skill development programs with a budget allocation of INR 10 crores annually.

These programs are designed to equip the youth of these communities with market-relevant skills.

Eligibility criteria for this scheme include being a member of the Sarna, Jahersthan, Hadgadi, or Masna communities.

Applicants must also be residents of the designated tribal areas.

There is no upper age limit for applicants.

However, applicants must be at least 18 years old to apply for financial assistance.

Income criteria stipulate that the annual family income should not exceed INR 2 lakhs.

Educational requirements are not strictly defined but preference is given to applicants with at least a primary education.

The application process involves several steps.

First, applicants must obtain the application form from the local tribal welfare office.

The form can also be downloaded from the official website of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs.

Applicants must fill out the form accurately and attach necessary documents.

Required documents include proof of identity such as an Aadhaar card.

Proof of residence is also required, which can be in the form of a ration card or utility bill.

Additionally, applicants must provide income certificates issued by the local revenue authority.

Once the application is complete, it must be submitted to the local tribal welfare office.

The application will then be reviewed by the designated committee.

The committee is responsible for verifying the eligibility of the applicants.

The timeline for processing applications is typically 30 days from the date of submission.

Disbursement of funds occurs within 15 days after the application is approved.

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Ministry of Tribal Affairs.

State governments also play a crucial role in the implementation of the scheme.

Each state has its own tribal welfare department that oversees the execution of the scheme.

Contact details for the Ministry of Tribal Affairs can be found on their official website.

The scheme is part of a broader initiative to empower tribal communities across India.

The government has allocated a total budget of INR 500 crores for the implementation of this scheme over five years.

This budget is aimed at ensuring that adequate resources are available for the various components of the scheme.

The scheme also includes provisions for health care services.

Health camps are organized in tribal areas to provide free medical check-ups and treatments.

These camps are conducted in collaboration with local health departments.

The aim is to improve the overall health indicators of these communities.

The scheme also promotes cultural preservation among these tribal groups.

Cultural programs and workshops are organized to celebrate and promote their heritage.

The government encourages the involvement of non-governmental organizations in the implementation of the scheme.

NGOs can assist in the outreach and awareness programs related to the scheme.

Monitoring and evaluation of the scheme are conducted regularly.

The Ministry of Tribal Affairs has established a framework for assessing the impact of the scheme.

Feedback from beneficiaries is collected to improve the scheme continuously.

The scheme is designed to be inclusive and participatory.

Community involvement is encouraged in the planning and execution of development activities.

The Sarna / Jahersthan / Hadgadi & Masna Protection and Development Scheme represents a significant step towards addressing the challenges faced by these tribal communities.

It aims to empower them economically and socially.

The government is committed to ensuring that the benefits of the scheme reach the intended beneficiaries.

Regular updates and reports on the progress of the scheme are published by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs.

These reports provide transparency and accountability in the implementation process.

The scheme is expected to create a positive impact on the livelihoods of thousands of families.

By focusing on education and skill development, the scheme aims to break the cycle of poverty.

The government encourages beneficiaries to utilize the financial assistance wisely.

This will help in creating sustainable livelihoods for their families.

Overall, the Sarna / Jahersthan / Hadgadi & Masna Protection and Development Scheme is a comprehensive effort to uplift marginalized tribal communities in India.
